question: Does the KC hidden-state mismatch precede the first accepted-event boundary difference near 1.482 ms, or appear across it?

rivals.A: Different event crossing time within the 1-2-ms interval creates the later hidden-state mismatch; pre-event 1-ms state should meet the frozen 1e-4 state limit.
rivals.B: Local independent-block versus global midpoint integration already changes hidden KC state before that event; pre-event 1-ms state fails the same limit.
rivals.C: A discarded predictor leaks into the next accepted state in one engine; accepted-event count alone cannot rule it out. Boundary and observer-neutrality tests may weaken but not isolate this without internal trial/restore instrumentation.

prototype: Two engines from the same checkpoint run 2ms sham; post-step KC somatic and axonal states are copied after ms 1 and 2. An otherwise identical no-capture run for each engine tests exact final-state neutrality. No biological intervention or parameter change.
control: For each engine, full final scientific state of capture-on/off must be bitwise equal before attributing any engine difference. Compare same array paths and IDs at 1ms and 2ms; count accepted events excluding the restored predictor and record first block disagreement. Apply the existing 1e-4 absolute state limit; do not alter it after observing data.
stop: Stop at first capture-on/off mismatch or domain/source failure; preserve prefixes. A KC difference at 1ms disfavors an event-only explanation but does not prove which integrator is biologically faithful. No stage-3 admission.
